name: pi-book
tagline: Source-backed architecture notes for building agents
description: pi-book is a technical book and set of architecture notes about building agents, grounded directly in source. Rather than hand-waving about agent design, it walks through real implementations and the reasoning behind them, making it a hands-on reference for anyone shipping an agent. It is written for practitioners who want to understand the internals — memory, tools, context wiring, and evaluation — well enough to build their own.
highlights: Source-backed notes tie agent concepts to concrete implementations
Covers the internals of building agents rather than just using them
A practical reference for practitioners and a useful onboarding ramp
Written in Vue, keeping the resource itself approachable to read
curatorNote: Everyone talks about building agents; few bother to trace the actual source. pi-book is that rare reference that grounds advice in real implementations, and it shows in how quickly it picked up stars.
